overview: This file concerns American official monitoring of Japan’s English-language press and its treatment of the United States in 1940–1941. Its principal item is Ambassador Joseph C. Grew’s August 1940 despatch transmitting three Japan Times cartoons about President Franklin D. Roosevelt and American policy; it also contains an April 1940 State Department memorandum on the financing, staffing, ownership, and political orientation of the Japan Times and Japan Advertiser. Later-filed material includes cross-reference sheets and a November 1941 telegram reproducing the American Embassy’s published denial that the United States had demanded Chinese naval bases and economic concessions. Collectively, the documents illuminate press propaganda, foreign influence over newspapers, worsening U.S.–Japanese relations, and the Embassy’s efforts to answer hostile or misleading publicity.

people.name: Joseph C. Grew
people.role: U.S. Ambassador to Japan; sender of the despatch and telegram

people.name: Toshi Go
people.role: Managing Director and Editor of the Japan Times from January 10, 1940

people.name: Coville
people.role: Division of Far Eastern Affairs staff member credited in the drafting notation

subfiles.title: Grew despatch transmitting three Japan Times cartoons
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Grew transmits and assesses three Japan Times cartoons concerning the United States and President Roosevelt.
subfiles.summary: Grew forwards three 1940 Japan Times cartoons; he finds Roosevelt's warning cartoon unobjectionable but calls the gasoline-to-Russia-not-Japan cartoon unpleasant, and objects to one implying the President is excessively talkative, given Japanese sensitivity about criticizing a chief of state.

subfiles.title: “Uncle Sam’s Shadow” cartoon
subfiles.about: A Japan Times cartoon presents the United States as being awakened by Roosevelt’s warning.
subfiles.summary: Enclosed Japan Times cartoon 'Uncle Sam's Shadow' shows the U.S. awakening to Roosevelt's warning; Grew considers it not especially objectionable.

subfiles.title: Cartoon portraying Roosevelt as a gasoline pump
subfiles.about: A Japan Times cartoon caricatures Roosevelt as dispensing gasoline to Russia while withholding it from Japan.
subfiles.summary: Surviving cartoon page (July 30, 1940) depicts Roosevelt's head on a gasoline pump, implying he let Russia but not Japan get gasoline; Grew calls it distinctly unpleasant.

subfiles.title: “Coast Defenses” cartoon
subfiles.from: The Japan Times, reproducing material attributed to the New York Herald Tribune
subfiles.about: The cartoon and accompanying note criticize Roosevelt’s alleged talkativeness and identify the New Deal as an opposition target.
subfiles.summary: Cartoon 'Coast Defenses,' from the anti-administration Herald Tribune, implies Roosevelt's talkativeness is a New Deal target; Grew finds the implication unpleasant.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to telegram on alleged American demands in China
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew (sender of referenced telegram)
subfiles.about: The sheet points to a telegram quoting the Embassy’s denial of rumors that the United States demanded four Chinese naval bases and economic concessions in return for aid.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Grew's telegram on an alleged American demand for four Chinese naval bases tied to Lend-Lease aid.

subfiles.title: Grew telegram reproducing Embassy denial of demands on China
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Grew transmits the text of an Embassy letter denying press allegations that the United States sought Chinese naval bases and economic domination.
subfiles.summary: Telegram reproduces the Embassy's letter denying a Japan Times editorial's claim that Washington sought exclusive postwar use of four naval bases and controlling economic measures in China, asking the editor to publicize the denial.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to telegram on hostile Japanese press tone
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew (sender of referenced telegram)
subfiles.about: The sheet refers researchers to Grew’s report of informal comments to the Japanese foreign minister about aggressive press treatment of the United States.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a telegram on the Japanese press's hostile tone toward the U.S. and Grew's remarks to the foreign minister.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on the English-language press in Tokyo
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State (drafting notation: Coville)
subfiles.about: The memorandum summarizes intelligence about the editorial direction, financing, staffing, and prospective ownership of Tokyo’s English-language newspapers.
subfiles.summary: Memo: under editor Toshi Go, the Japan Times courted American opinion with higher-paid American staff, allegedly subsidized ¥7,000 monthly by the Foreign Office; sources also described Asahi's interest in buying the Japan Advertiser and German/British purchase offers.

interest: Shows 1940-41 Japan Times cartoons offending Grew, plus press-rebuttal and media-acquisition intelligence before Pearl Harbor.
